newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel for sale of gas, food, tourism shares.
newsitem.headline: India panel for sale of gas, food, tourism shares.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission, which oversees partial privatisation, on Thursday recommended the sale of shares in three state firms and the setting up of a pool to club funds raised by divestment.

It said the government should sell 25 percent of its stake in the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), 100 percent of Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd and 74 percent or more of the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC).

"The commission has recommended that the proceeds of disinvestment be placed separately in a Disinvestment Fund and not be fungible with other government receipts," G.V. Ramakrishna, the commission's chairman told a news conference.
Ramakrishna said he had submitted the first report of the commission, which was set up last year, to Industry Minister Murasoli Maran earlier on Thursday.
"In this report, we have recommended disinvestment in three different public sector undertakings (PSUs)," Ramakrisha said.
He said the Commission had also recommended that a high-level government panel, called the Standing Empowered Group, be set-up to oversee the sell-off of shares.
"As a general principle, we have also suggested that where appropriate PSUs should be restructured before disinvestment in order to improve efficiency and intrinsic share value," Ramakrishna said.
He said the Commission had also recommended more freedom for state-owned firms, including the induction of professionals on their board of directors.
The government has set a target of raising 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) in 1996/97 (April-March) from divestment, or the sale of partial stakes in state-controlled firms.
Last year India raised 3.57 billion rupees ($99.7 million) from divestment, well short of its target of 70 billion ($1.95 billion).

India had planned to sell a seven percent stake in telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in crude oil refining company Indian Oil Corp (IOC) in the first round of divestment in 1996/97.
But the government has not yet fixed a date for kicking off the first round of divestment.
The government plans a second tranche after the first round of sell-offs in VSNL and IOC, but time is running out before the 1996/97 year ends on March 31.
The Commission will not be in charge of the first two rounds. The Commission has been asked by the government to advise on 40 state-owned units for a third round of sell-offs.
Ramakrishna said the Commission would be making its next recommendation on more state-owned firms in March.
"We hope to complete the process by September-October," he said.
